harbour.intro: Harbour is big: 140+ screens and 11 flows, built from scratch. AI did the slow first drafts, so my time went on the decisions.
steps: Read import rules, ferry schedules and 30+ competitor pages, and turned my interview notes into themes and quotes I could check.
Drafted the 11 flows from the job stages. I checked every branch against how importers really work and cut half of the steps.
A clickable job workspace and live map in a day, so importers could react to something real before I drew a single final screen.
Realistic VINs, routes, invoices and empty, error and loading states for every table, so no screen shipped with lorem ipsum.
harbour.rule: Every flow, number and label was checked against real import jobs before it reached a screen. The model wrote drafts; the calls were mine.

strata.intro: Strata has 244 screens across many sites. AI took the repetitive work, so I could spend time on the content model and the publish flow.
steps: Compared how 20+ CMS tools handle shared content and summarised interview notes into pains and quotes.
Drafted page types, fields and inheritance rules. I tested each one against real partner sites and kept the ones that held.
A working publish-to-many-sites prototype in a day, used in the first round of user calls.
Generated realistic page lists, site names and every empty, error and conflict state for 244 screens.
strata.rule: The content model was never left to a model. Each rule about what a site can override was argued out with the developers.

inner-glow.intro: Inner Glow is an AI product, so I used AI to design it too: to research, to write the coach's voice and to test it early.
steps: Reviewed mood-tracker reviews and studies on habit drop-off, and grouped them into the reasons people stop after a week.
Wrote and tested dozens of coach replies to set the tone: warm, short, never clinical. The best ones became the content guide.
A clickable check-in and insight flow in a day, tested with five people before the final design.
Drafted mood copy, insight cards and calm background art, then refined it by hand to match the brand.
inner-glow.rule: In a mental-health app, tone is the product. Every line the coach says was read by a person and checked against what the app can safely say.

jbc.intro: JBC sells long, high-value projects. AI helped me understand the audience fast and get the project pages right before design.
steps: Studied how 25+ venue and fit-out firms present their work, and what investors look for before they call.
Drafted the sitemap and the case page outline. I reworked it around proof first: scale, timeline, results.
A clickable project page in a day, so the client could react to the story before the visuals.
Drafted project summaries from the client's notes, then edited them down to plain, short lines.
jbc.rule: Investors check the facts, so I did too: every project figure, date and client name came from JBC, not from a prompt.

dalitis.intro: Dalitis has three audiences and many listings. AI helped me sort the audience, structure the listings and write clear copy.
steps: Compared 20+ Cyprus developer sites and grouped what homebuyers, investors and businesses each look for first.
Drafted the sitemap and listing filters. I tested them against the real portfolio and merged what overlapped.
A clickable listings and project page in a day, reviewed with the sales team.
Turned long project notes into short listing descriptions in one tone, then edited them by hand.
dalitis.rule: Prices, sizes and availability come straight from the client’s data. AI helped me write about the homes, never decide what they cost.

thallo.intro: Thallo was not built yet, so the site had to sell a picture. AI helped me research tenants and show the space before it existed.
steps: Looked at how office buildings in Limassol and abroad are let, and what companies ask before a viewing.
Drafted the page story: location, floors, specs, contact. I reordered it around the questions tenants ask first.
A clickable floor-picker in a day, so the agents could try it before the final design.
Mood images for the lobby and terraces to set the direction, plus short spec copy. Final images came from the architect's renders.
thallo.rule: AI images showed the mood, not the building. On the live site every view is the architect’s real render or plan.

pcela.intro: Pcela is about speed for the buyer, so I used AI to move fast too: research, checkout flow and product copy.
steps: Reviewed 20+ flower shops and 200+ customer reviews, and grouped the reasons people drop out of checkout.
Drafted the bouquet-to-checkout flow. I cut it down to three steps on mobile.
A clickable mobile checkout in a day, tested with five people on their own phones.
Wrote bouquet names, short descriptions and every delivery and error message, then edited them for tone.
pcela.rule: Faster for me, never at the buyer’s cost: delivery times, slots and prices follow the shop’s own rules.

platon-suites.intro: A 36-page print brochure has a lot of words and many pages to lay out. AI helped with research, copy and early directions.
steps: Studied how off-plan homes in Limassol are sold and what buyers ask before they reserve.
Drafted the 36-page story and the page plan. I reworked it to open with the area, then the homes.
Early mood images for the moodboard and the first direction. The final brochure uses the real renders.
Drafted text for every spread from the developer's notes, then edited it down to short lines in one tone.
platon-suites.rule: Print is final, so nothing went to the printer unchecked: areas, prices and specs came from the developer, and every page was proofread by hand.
